chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) said:

I asked him about a man who designated the price of a female slave as a sacrificial offering (hady) for the Kaaba. He said: 'How should he act?' He said: 'Indeed, a man came to my father, and he had designated his female slave as a hady for the Kaaba. So my father said to him:

key_terms.الْأَوَّلَ فَالْأَوَّلَ: The first one then the first one (one by one)
key_terms.الْحِجْر: Al-Hijr (a specific area near the Kaaba)
key_terms.فُلَانَ: So-and-so (a placeholder name for the man in question)
key_terms.لِلْكَعْبَةِ: For the Kaaba (the sacred house in Mecca)
key_terms.هَدْيًا: Sacrificial offering (animal or value) brought to the Kaaba during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a man who makes a female slave a sacrificial offering for the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) illustrates the practical application of 'hady' (sacrificial offering) through charitable distribution rather than animal slaughter, reflecting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding vows. The specific instruction to announce in the Hijr area highlights the social dimension of fulfilling religious obligations by targeting the needy directly, ensuring the offering serves both spiritual and communal welfare purposes.
